title: Dependency Clarity huddle — Product / Eng / Applied ML prep & follow-ups
content:
Goal: get to a single clear dependency map + next-step owner list for Q3 features that touch model onboarding, runtime changes, and console rollouts.

Context / why this huddle: product has a set of target milestones (model ver pinning, rollout window, cost targets). Eng needs to know which runtime changes are blockers vs nice-to-have. Applied ML (research) needs clear gating on evals and regression thresholds before we flip traffic. Too many half-overlapping tasks — want explicit owners and minimal gating.

Attendees (tentative): Camila (note), Arjun (Eng - serving runtime), Sofia (Product - hosted API), Marcus (Applied ML), Priya (Console PM), optional: Evan (SRE on routing), Lina (Release eng on rollout automation)

Primary outcomes I want from the 30–45m huddle:
- A prioritized list of 6 concrete dependencies (ranked) with single-point owner and 'blocker?' flag
- For each dependency: explicit acceptance criteria (what must be true before rollout can proceed)
- A short timeline (3 checkpoints over 6 weeks) and who signs each checkpoint
- A small set of follow-up actions (max 8) with owners and dates

Agenda (rough)
1) Quick framing (2–3m) — scope, no scope, timebox
2) Walk dependency list (20m) — surface unknowns; mark blocker vs non-blocker
3) Acceptance criteria workshop (10m) — group edits to short criteria per dependency
4) Timeline/handshake (5–7m) — who will verify, fallback plan if a gate misses date
5) Confirm actions, owners, deadlines (3–5m)

Dependency list (first pass) — label, why it matters, probable owner, initial blocker?
A. Model quantization profile for p3-small-compatible variant — affects cost target; owner: Marcus; blocker: yes (if quality delta > 1.5% on evaluators)
B. Runtime kernel swap for long-sequence attention (v2 kernel) — speed uplift for long-context customers; owner: Arjun; blocker: maybe (depends on perf regression risk)
C. Console UI for per-route rollout controls (canary % + auto-fallback) — supports product rollouts; owner: Priya; blocker: no (can be phased)
D. Eval-suite automation for prompt-preserving regression checks — ensures model parity after quantization; owner: Marcus + Sofia; blocker: yes (until we have passable coverage)
E. Metric telemetry hook for token-level cost attribution per model variant — needed for post-rollout cost verification; owner: Arjun (infra) + Sofia (product metrics); blocker: maybe
F. Canary traffic routing policy integration with Dedicated pools — required for enterprise customers' fallbacks; owner: Evan (SRE) + Priya; blocker: yes for Dedicated customers

Acceptance criteria (draft suggestions)
- A: Quantization profile considered OK if top-1 exact-match delta <= 1.0% on target eval set AND no clear hallucination regression on the 30-case golden prompts list.
- B: Kernel v2 must show p95 latency <= current p95 * 0.9 on baseline long-seq demo and not increase memory tail errors; unit tests for kv-cache retained.
- C: Console controls present for alpha (canary %, ttl, fallback route) and tested end-to-end in staging; rollout UI hidden by flag until after smoke tests.
- D: Regression suite to run in CI on PRs to quantization branch, with a pass/fail threshold defined and automated blamelist notification.
- E: Telemetry shows per-model per-route token cost within 1 hour of rollout; historical baseline available to compare.
- F: Routing policy to support cluster-priority and fallback rules; simulated failover must show <2s routing error window in staging.

Open questions / uncertainties I want us to call out in the meeting
- Do we accept a slightly higher latency for long sequences in exchange for 20% cost savings? (tradeoff discussion — bring data)
- Which customers must be excluded from early quantized variants? Who signs customer-exclusion list?
- Is there appetite to delay console GA until after Dedicated rollout? (product decision)
- Are current eval datasets representative of production prompts? Marcus: bring sample up-to-date results.

Data prep (asks before the meeting) — assigned
- Marcus: upload top-line quantization run (metrics table + 30 golden prompts examples) to the Confluence page (CONFLUENCE-PLAT-4567) by EOD tomorrow.
- Arjun: perf numbers for kernel v2 vs v1 on the long-seq harness (p50/p95/p99) — short CSV + link to perf Jenkins job.
- Priya: draft of console rollout feature toggles and acceptance test plan.
- Sofia: product priority matrix showing which customers/features require strict SLAs vs flexible cost tradeoffs.

Proposed timeline (6 weeks) — checkpoints
- Week 1 (this week): finalize owners and acceptance criteria; blockers flagged.
- Week 3: intermediate checkpoint — quantization v1 candidate + kernel v2 smoke tests in staging; telemetry hooks deployed to staging.
- Week 6: sign-off window for limited canary to 5% internal traffic + selected enterprise customers; go/no-go decision meeting scheduled.

Follow-up actions (write down as we leave the meeting) — my initial list (will convert to tickets)
1) Marcus: Upload quantization eval artifacts and short doc on limitations — due 2026-07-07
2) Arjun: Create kernel-v2 PR with perf notes + mark known risks in PR description — due 2026-07-09
3) Priya: Prototype console canary controls PR and e2e tests — due 2026-07-12
4) Evan: Draft routing fallback runbook for Dedicated pools and schedule failover drill — due 2026-07-10
5) Sofia: Compile product-customer exclusion list & priority matrix — due 2026-07-08
6) Camila (me): consolidate meeting notes, create a single dependency spreadsheet, and circulate for review — due 2026-07-03
7) Team: schedule go/no-go on calendar (6-week check) — owner: Priya + Arjun — due 2026-07-02

Risks to call out during the huddle
- Overly broad acceptance criteria that allow silent regressions
- Missing telemetry causing us to blindly roll out and only notice cost drift post-facto
- Too many simultaneous changes (kernel + quant + routing) leading to indistinguishable failure modes

Fallbacks / mitigation suggestions
- Stagger rollouts: quantization + kernel swaps not in same canary window unless both pass staging smoke tests.
- Keep a short 'rollback play' documented and rehearsed for first week post-canary.
- Predefine a minimal set of user-facing checks (latency, top-1 quality on golden prompts, token-cost delta) that must be green within 1 hour of canary start.

Notes for facilitation (me as host)
- Keep the group to 6 people max in main discussion — pull others into side 1:1s if needed.
- Use a shared Google Sheet live-edit during the meeting for dependency ranking (I will create and share).
- Be strict on time for the acceptance criteria step (we can capture wording and iterate after meeting).

Post-meeting immediate deliverables (what I will do right after)
- Convert the dependency list into a single Google Sheet with columns: dependency, owner, blocker?, acceptance criteria (text), ticket link, due date.
- Create short follow-up email summarizing owners and immediate asks; push to Slack #xfunc-roadmap with @mentions.
- Open JIRA epics for any new engineering work that is still missing a ticket.

Conversation prompts (quick lines to use to move the room)
- "If this is blocked, what is the smallest test we can ship to reduce risk?"
- "Who signs the quality gate for this item?"
- "Can we agree on a 3-point checklist that if green, we consider the canary healthy?"

Timing: propose Fri 2026-07-02 09:30 PT (30–45m). If that doesn't work, early Mon morning.

Misc scratch (to delete before final):
- Consider adding a 'regression champion' to own golden prompts long-term.
- Check if Burke's team already has token-cost dashboards we can reuse.

---
End of notes. Will iterate after meeting and convert to tickets + sheet.
